summary: Legacy runtime repair consistently returns typed 422 refusals for unavailable native proof and refuses procfs mounts that can hide live producers

replay.detail: No projection replay or new repair authority.

schema.detail: No database or replicated claim schema changes.

rules.detail: No claim admission, checkpoint or projection rule changes. Native closure capture now requires complete procfs visibility before process ownership checks or enumeration.

compatibility.detail: Dry-run, apply and doctor consistently return legacy-start-proof-unavailable (HTTP 422) when native capture cannot prove closure. Process-read details contain only stage, pid and numeric errno when available, never raw environment or native error paths. Procfs that can hide processes refuses with stage procfs-visibility and reason procfs-hides-processes, including mount options: any hidepid value other than 0/off (including 1, 2, invisible, noaccess and ptraceable), or subset=pid. Unreadable, malformed or missing mount evidence refuses with the same type and a distinct reason. Ordinary procfs behavior is unchanged.

downtime.detail: Normal daemon rollout; no migration, projection replay or rebuild.

manual.detail: No automatic configuration changes. Hosts whose procfs can hide processes cannot use legacy-start repair until complete visibility is established. Inaccessible live process evidence never becomes cleanup authority.

recovery.detail: Refusal changes neither runtime nor store state. No process exclusions or destructive recovery. Earlier binaries do not enforce the procfs visibility precondition.
